dataset.dataset: DuoRC ParaphraseRC complete-plot extractive subset with native no-answer labels
dataset.citation: Saha, Aralikatte, Khapra, Sankaranarayanan (2018). DuoRC: Towards Complex Language Understanding with Paraphrased Reading Comprehension. ACL. arXiv:1804.07927.
dataset.policy: Official train/dev/test map to local train/validation/test. Movie IDs, exact complete contexts and question IDs are disjoint across splits. All historical manifest IDs and contexts are excluded from every split. Native no_answer is preserved; negative targets are NOT_FOUND with empty references. Positive supervision derives literal exact offsets with both tokenizer budgets and exact reader token boundaries. Full original answer lists remain scoring references. Identical question text within one movie is deduplicated; at most four distinct questions per movie are selected by a seeded balanced integer-flow allocation. No model outputs influence eligibility or sampling.
dataset.balance: Exactly half answerable and half native missing-answer examples. Short/long groups are descriptive, not equally weighted; complete ParaphraseRC plots contain too few short answerable questions for the earlier four-way quota.
dataset.span_policy: Offsets are derived from exact source gold strings, not supplied natively by DuoRC. All eligible exact occurrences are stored; the earliest start/end/text is the deterministic training target. A source answer with no eligible literal span is excluded, never relabeled missing. Original answers, complete context and question remain unchanged.
dataset.sampling: Seeded shuffle of sorted movie IDs and each movie/class question pool; integer max-flow from balanced class quotas through per-movie capacities, followed by a seeded selected-row shuffle. Split seeds are seed, seed+1, seed+2.
limitations: Filtered historical movie-plot corpus, not native answerability prevalence or unseen real-world documents.
Multiple questions share a movie context within a split; uncertainty should resample movies as clusters.
The QA reader was initialized from SQuAD2 training. Base-model pretraining exposure and cross-corpus near duplicates cannot be ruled out.
DuoRC includes paraphrased/abstractive answers. Requiring one short literal span narrows the task; full original answer lists are still used for scoring.
Repository MIT notice is recorded; source plots originate from IMDb and Wikipedia. Raw plots/questions/references stay in ignored local artifacts.
Complete contexts must fit both models. No cropping, sliding windows, answer deletion, generated negatives or model-based filtering is used.

reader_source.previous_training: Publisher fine-tuned on SQuAD2 using a GPU; current experiment adapts and infers on CPU only.

limitations: Fresh filtered DuoRC movie plots, not the full corpus or arbitrary documents; human answers require at least one bounded exact literal span for eligibility.
Multiple questions per movie are clustered; answerability is balanced, passage lengths are not.
Reader and generator have unequal prior supervision. The publisher reader was trained on SQuAD2 on a GPU; only this adaptation/inference stage is CPU-only.
Historical public data may have appeared in model pretraining; exact exclusions cannot prove absence of semantic contamination.
Only initial and one final reader checkpoint are considered. Fixed thresholds and selection use validation only.
